akhfash:18-18.t: He said ﴿فَأَنَّىٰ لَهُمْ إِذَا جَآءَتْهُمْ ذِكْرَاهُمْ﴾: He means "how will their reminder avail them when the Hour has come to them?"

akhfash:22-22.t: And He said ﴿فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ أَن تُفْسِدُواْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: the first (إن تولّيتم) is for the conditional, and you made ﴿عَسَيْتُمْ﴾ fall on ﴿أَن تُفْسِدُواْ﴾ because it is a noun. ﴿عَسَيْتُمْ﴾ or "عَسَيْتُ" cannot operate on it unless "أنْ" is in it; you do not say "عَسَيْتُم الفِعْلَ" (you might the deed). Just as in your saying "لو ان زيدا جاء كان خيرا له" (if Zayd had come it would have been better for him), your saying "أَنَّ زَيْداً جاءَ" is a noun, yet you do not say "لوذاك" (if that), because not all nouns occur in every position, and not all verbs fall on all nouns. Do you not see that they say "يَدَعُ" (he leaves) but do not say "وَدَعَ", [and they say "يَذَرُ"] but do not say "وَذَر"?

akhfash:35-35.t: And He said ﴿وَلَن يَتِرَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ﴾, i.e. in your deeds, as you say: "دَخَلْتُ البيتَ" (I entered the house) while meaning "into the house".

akhfash:38-38.t: And He said ﴿هَا أَنتُمْ هَـٰؤُلاَءِ﴾: He put the alerting particle (hā) in two places for emphasis, and the alerting in "هَؤُلاَءِ" is a permanent alerting.

daas-irab:1-3.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَصَدُّوا﴾ conjoined to kafarū. ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَضَلَّ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ its object; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of alladhīna, and the nominal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾ conjoined to āmanū. ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَآمَنُوا﴾ conjoined. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what precedes them. ﴿نُزِّلَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿عَلى مُحَمَّدٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ its khabar. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial); the nominal clause is parenthetical and has no grammatical position. ﴿كَفَّرَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سَيِّئاتِهِمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of alladhīna. ﴿وَأَصْلَحَ بالَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to kaffara ʿanhum. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِأَنَّ﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition, and anna is a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its noun. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the ṣila. ﴿اتَّبَعُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of anna. ﴿الْباطِلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; anna and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبَعُوا الْحَقَّ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿يَضْرِبُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿أَمْثالَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:4-6.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and idhā is an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿لَقِيتُمُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فَضَرْبَ﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿الرِّقابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of beginning (ibtidāʾ). ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿أَثْخَنْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿فَشُدُّوا﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الْوَثاقَ﴾ its object; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَإِمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption and of consequence (tafrīʿ), and immā is a particle of condition and of detailing (tafṣīl). ﴿مَنًّا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb. ﴿بَعْدُ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿وَإِمَّا فِداءً﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿حَتَّى تَضَعَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after ḥattā. ﴿الْحَرْبُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿أَوْزارَها﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by ḥattā, and they [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to (mutaʿalliq) fidāʾ. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and law is a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil; the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿لَانْتَصَرَ﴾ the lām falls in the apodosis of the condition, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative (muhmal). ﴿لِيَبْلُوَا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an implicit an after the lām of causation (taʿlīl), with its fāʿil latent. ﴿بَعْضَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِبَعْضٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the interpreted maṣdar from an and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and they are attached to an implied, omitted verb. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿قُتِلُوا﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a ḍamma (اللَّهُ); as muḍāf ilayhi it is اللَّهِ.] ﴿فَلَنْ﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and lan is a particle causing the accusative. ﴿يُضِلَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by lan, its fāʿil latent. ﴿أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿سَيَهْدِيهِمْ﴾ the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَيُصْلِحُ بالَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to sa-yahdīhim. ﴿وَيُدْخِلُهُمُ﴾ conjoined to sa-yahdīhim. ﴿الْجَنَّةَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَرَّفَها﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the verbal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of al-janna.

daas-irab:7-11.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ yā is a vocative particle, hā is for drawing attention (tanbīh), and ayy is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ badal (substitute). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿تَنْصُرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَنْصُرْكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the kāf is its object and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَيُثَبِّتْ أَقْدامَكُمْ﴾ conjoined to yanṣurkum. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فَتَعْساً﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) taʿsan. ﴿وَأَضَلَّ أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ a preposition, and anna and its noun. ﴿كَرِهُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause karihū is the khabar (predicate) of anna. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنْزَلَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from anna and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and they [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿فَأَحْبَطَ أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to karihū. ﴿أَفَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and lam is a particle causing the jussive. ﴿يَسِيرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَيَنْظُرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿كَيْفَ كانَ﴾ an interrogative noun, the fronted khabar of kāna. ﴿عاقِبَةُ﴾ its postponed noun. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted [element that is the] ṣila of the relative noun; the clause kāna stands in place of the object of yanẓurū. ﴿دَمَّرَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلِلْكافِرِينَ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿أَمْثالُها﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلَى﴾ anna, its noun and its khabar. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of alladhīna, and the interpreted maṣdar from anna and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and they are attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَأَنَّ الْكافِرِينَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation, which works like inna. ﴿مَوْلَى﴾ its noun. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar; the nominal clause is the khabar of anna.

daas-irab:12-14.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿يُدْخِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its object; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ conjoined to āmanū. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of jannāt. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يَتَمَتَّعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of alladhīna. ﴿وَيَأْكُلُونَ﴾ conjoined to yatamattaʿūna. ﴿كَما﴾ the kāf is a particle of comparison and of the genitive, and mā is maṣdariyya (yielding a verbal noun). ﴿تَأْكُلُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الْأَنْعامُ﴾ fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from mā and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and they [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَالنَّارُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿مَثْوىً﴾ its khabar. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to mathwan; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and kaʾayyin is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿قَرْيَةٍ﴾ tamyīz (specification), genitive in form. ﴿هِيَ أَشَدُّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿قُوَّةً﴾ tamyīz; the clause kaʾayyin is resumptive, and the clause hiya ashaddu is an adjective of qarya. ﴿مِنْ قَرْيَتِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ashaddu. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ an adjective of qaryatika. ﴿أَخْرَجَتْكَ﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَهْلَكْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the khabar of kaʾayyin. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and lā is the lā of generic negation, which works like inna. ﴿ناصِرَ﴾ its noun. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَفَمَنْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and man is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; its noun is latent. ﴿عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar of kāna; the verbal clause is the ṣila, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of bayyina. ﴿كَمَنْ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ man. ﴿زُيِّنَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سُوءُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿عَمَلِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the verbal clause is the ṣila of man. ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَهْواءَهُمْ﴾ its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:15-16.t: ﴿مَثَلُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْجَنَّةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الَّتِي﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of al-janna. ﴿وُعِدَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿الْمُتَّقُونَ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فِيها﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿أَنْهارٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ ماءٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, an adjective of anhār. ﴿غَيْرِ﴾ an adjective. ﴿آسِنٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause fīhā anhār is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ mathal. ﴿وَأَنْهارٌ مِنْ لَبَنٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam. ﴿طَعْمُهُ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is an adjective of laban. ﴿وَأَنْهارٌ مِنْ خَمْرٍ﴾ also conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَذَّةٍ﴾ an adjective of khamr. ﴿لِلشَّارِبِينَ﴾ an adjective of ladhdha. ﴿وَأَنْهارٌ مِنْ عَسَلٍ مُصَفًّى﴾ conjoined to the one before it. ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and lahum is a fronted khabar. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, an adjective of the omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿الثَّمَراتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَمَغْفِرَةٌ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and maghfira is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, an adjective of maghfira. ﴿كَمَنْ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُوَ خالِدٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is the ṣila of man. ﴿فِي النَّارِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to khālid. ﴿وَسُقُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿ماءٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a kasra (ماءٍ); in the verse it is the accusative ماءً.] ﴿حَمِيماً﴾ an adjective of māʾ; the clause is conjoined to the ṣila clause. ﴿فَقَطَّعَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَمْعاءَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and minhum is a fronted khabar. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿يَسْتَمِعُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of beginning (ibtidāʾ). ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿خَرَجُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the apodosis of a condition that does not cause the jussive. ﴿أُوتُوا﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿الْعِلْمَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿ماذا﴾ a mubtadaʾ and khabar. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila, on the view that dhā is a relative noun. ﴿آنِفاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿طَبَعَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْواءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:17-19.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿اهْتَدَوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿زادَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its first object, with its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿هُدىً﴾ its second object; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَآتاهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object, its fāʿil being latent. ﴿تَقْواهُمْ﴾ its second object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and hal is an interrogative particle. ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿السَّاعَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the hāʾ is its object. ﴿بَغْتَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of al-sāʿa. ﴿فَقَدْ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of causation (taʿlīl), and qad is a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿جاءَ أَشْراطُها﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is causal and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَأَنَّى﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and annā is an interrogative noun, the fronted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "deliverance" (al-khalāṣ). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿جاءَتْهُمْ ذِكْراهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its object and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَاعْلَمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿لا إِلهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ﴾ its i'rab has preceded in verse 8 of al-Dukhān; the nominal clause is the khabar of anna, the interpreted maṣdar from anna and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of iʿlam, and the clause iʿlam is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿لِذَنْبِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿مُتَقَلَّبَكُمْ﴾ its object. ﴿وَمَثْواكُمْ﴾ conjoined to it; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:20-23.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and an imperfect verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of alladhīna. ﴿لَوْلا﴾ a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿نُزِّلَتْ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿سُورَةٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and idhā is an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿أُنْزِلَتْ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿سُورَةٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿مُحْكَمَةٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَذُكِرَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿فِيهَا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْقِتالُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿رَأَيْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its object; the clause is the apodosis of a condition that does not cause the jussive, and has no grammatical position. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مَرَضٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿نَظَرَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿الْمَغْشِيِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to al-maghshiyy. ﴿مِنَ الْمَوْتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to it. ﴿فَأَوْلى﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and awlā is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of the past, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to it. ﴿طاعَةٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted. ﴿وَقَوْلٌ﴾ conjoined to ṭāʿa. ﴿مَعْرُوفٌ﴾ an adjective of qawl. ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and idhā is an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿عَزَمَ الْأَمْرُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿فَلَوْ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle falling in the apodosis of idhā, and law is a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿صَدَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿لَكانَ﴾ the lām falls in the apodosis of law, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent. ﴿خَيْراً﴾ its khabar. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to khayran; the clause la-kāna is the apodosis of law and has no grammatical position. [Translator's note: the source reads «جواب لولا محل لها», evidently «جواب لو لا محل لها» run together.] ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and hal is an interrogative particle. ﴿عَسَيْتُمْ﴾ ʿasā and its noun. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿تَوَلَّيْتُمْ﴾ a past verb, and the tāʾ is its fāʿil; the clause is initial and has no grammatical position, and the clause ʿasaytum is resumptive. ﴿أَنْ تُفْسِدُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَتُقَطِّعُوا أَرْحامَكُمْ﴾ conjoined to an tufsidū; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is the khabar of ʿasā. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَعَنَهُمُ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فَأَصَمَّهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَعْمى أَبْصارَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to fa-aṣammahum.

daas-irab:24-28.t: ﴿أَفَلا﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and lā is negative. ﴿يَتَدَبَّرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْقُرْآنَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction in the sense of bal. ﴿عَلى قُلُوبٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿أَقْفالُها﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿ارْتَدُّوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلى أَدْبارِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to the verb. ﴿ما﴾ maṣdariyya (yielding a verbal noun). ﴿تَبَيَّنَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْهُدَى﴾ its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from mā and the verb is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿الشَّيْطانُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿سَوَّلَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿وَأَمْلى لَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to sawwala lahum. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar from anna and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿كَرِهُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of alladhīna. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿نَزَّلَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of mā. ﴿سَنُطِيعُكُمْ﴾ the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فِي بَعْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْأَمْرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِسْرارَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an interrogative noun, the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿تَوَفَّتْهُمُ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿يَضْرِبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿وُجُوهَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَدْبارَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to wujūhahum; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمُ اتَّبَعُوا﴾ see verse 26. ﴿ما أَسْخَطَ﴾ mā is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَكَرِهُوا رِضْوانَهُ فَأَحْبَطَ أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:29-31.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction. ﴿حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مَرَضٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a particle resembling the verb, lightened from the heavy anna; its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted. ﴿لَنْ يُخْرِجَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by lan. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿أَضْغانَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar of an, and an and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that stands in place of the two objects of ḥasiba. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and law is a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿نَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿لَأَرَيْناكَهُمْ﴾ the lām falls in the apodosis of the condition, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the kāf is its first object and the hāʾ its second object; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَلَعَرَفْتَهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, the lām falls in the apodosis of law, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿بِسِيماهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلَتَعْرِفَنَّهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the lām falls in the answer to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; its fāʿil is latent and the hāʾ is its object; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿فِي لَحْنِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْقَوْلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَعْمالَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the lām falls in the answer to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and its object, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of causation (taʿlīl) and of the genitive. ﴿نَعْلَمَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an implicit an after ḥattā, its fāʿil latent. ﴿الْمُجاهِدِينَ﴾ its object; an and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of the genitive by ḥattā, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to what precedes them; the clause la-nabluwannakum is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to al-mujāhidīn. ﴿وَالصَّابِرِينَ﴾ conjoined to al-mujāhidīn. ﴿وَنَبْلُوَا﴾ conjoined to naʿlama. ﴿أَخْبارَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:32-34.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَصَدُّوا﴾ conjoined to kafarū. ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَشَاقُّوا الرَّسُولَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِنْ﴾ ﴿بَعْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to shāqqū. ﴿ما﴾ maṣdariyya (yielding a verbal noun). ﴿تَبَيَّنَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to it. ﴿الْهُدى﴾ its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from mā and the verb is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿لَنْ يَضُرُّوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by lan, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a kasra (اللَّهِ); as mafʿūl bihi it is اللَّهَ.] ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq, standing in for an absolute object). ﴿وَسَيُحْبِطُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ refer to verse no. 7. ﴿أَطِيعُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا تُبْطِلُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿أَعْمالَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ see verse no. 34. [Translator's note: so in the source; this is verse 34 itself, and the parallel analysis is in verse 32 above.] ﴿وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿ماتُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is circumstantial. ﴿فَلَنْ يَغْفِرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by lan, and the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a kasra (اللَّهِ); as fāʿil it is اللَّهُ.] ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause inna alladhīna is initial.

daas-irab:35-37.t: ﴿فَلا تَهِنُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَتَدْعُوا﴾ conjoined to tahinū. ﴿إِلَى السَّلْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَأَنْتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ a conjunction, and the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿مَعَكُمْ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَلَنْ يَتِرَكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by lan; the kāf is its first object and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَعْمالَكُمْ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّمَا﴾ a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿الْحَياةُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿لَعِبٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿وَلَهْوٌ﴾ conjoined to laʿib; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and in causes the jussive. ﴿تُؤْمِنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ conjoined to tuʾminū. ﴿يُؤْتِكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); its fāʿil is latent and the kāf is its first object. ﴿أُجُورَكُمْ﴾ its second object; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَلا يَسْئَلْكُمْ أَمْوالَكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, lā is negative, and yasʾalkum amwālakum is conjoined to yuʾtikum ujūrakum. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿يَسْئَلْكُمُوها﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the protasis; its fāʿil is latent, the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi and hā the second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is initial. ﴿فَيُحْفِكُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb conjoined to yasʾalkumūhā. ﴿تَبْخَلُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَيُخْرِجْ﴾ conjoined to tabkhalū. ﴿أَضْغانَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:38-38.t: ﴿ها﴾ for drawing attention (tanbīh). ﴿أَنْتُمْ هؤُلاءِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿تُدْعَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِتُنْفِقُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by the implicit an after the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) tudʿawna. ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَمِنْكُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption and of consequence (tafrīʿ), and minkum is a fronted khabar. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿يَبْخَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and man is a conditional noun causing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَبْخَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿فَإِنَّما﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and innamā is a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿يَبْخَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَنْ نَفْسِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَاللَّهُ الْغَنِيُّ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ and al-ghaniyy its khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَأَنْتُمُ الْفُقَراءُ﴾ conjoined to Allāhu al-ghaniyy. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and in is a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿تَتَوَلَّوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the protasis, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is initial. ﴿يَسْتَبْدِلْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿قَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿غَيْرَكُمْ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَكُونُوا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive, and its noun. ﴿أَمْثالَكُمْ﴾ its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَضَرْبَ ٱلرِّقَابِ﴾.
Accusative as a command, and what puts it in the accusative is implied; and likewise every command in which you make the nouns overt and leave out the verbs: put the nouns in it in the accusative. It is mentioned that it is a discipline from Allah and a teaching to the believers for fighting.
His saying: ﴿فَإِمَّا مَنًّا بَعْدُ وَإِمَّا فِدَآءً﴾.
Also accusative by an implied verb: "either you show grace (تمنّوا) or you take ransom (تفدوا)". Al-mann is that you release the captive without ransom, and al-fidāʾ is that the captive ransoms himself.
His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ تَضَعَ ٱلْحَرْبُ أَوْزَارَهَا﴾.
Its sins and its shirk, until none remains but a Muslim or one at peace. The hāʾ in أوزارها may be for the war, while you mean the burdens of its people; and it may be for the people of shirk specifically, as in your saying: "until the war removes the burdens of the polytheists".
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ وَلَوْ يَشَآءُ اللَّهُ لاَنْتَصَرَ مِنْهُمْ﴾.
By angels other than you; and it is said: without fighting; but that He may test some of you by others, the believer by the unbeliever and the unbelief by the believer.
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ قَاتَلوا فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim and Zayd ibn Thābit read it ([Muḥammad narrated to us:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Khurāsānī narrated that to me, from [ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū] ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Zayd ibn Thābit): قاتَلوا; and al-Ḥasan read it: قُتِّلوا, doubled; and some lightened it, saying: قُتِلوا, light; and all of that is correct.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيُدْخِلُهُمُ ٱلْجَنَّةَ عَرَّفَهَا لَهُمْ﴾.
They will know their dwellings when they enter it, so that one of them will know his dwelling in Paradise better than he knows his home when he returns from the Friday prayer.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿فَتَعْساً لَّهُمْ وَأَضَلَّ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾.
It is as though He said: "so Allah has made them wretched and caused their deeds to go astray", because an imprecation may be treated like a command or a prohibition. Do you not see that أضل is a verb, and it is referred back to التعس, which is a noun, because there is in it the meaning of "He made them wretched (أتعسهم)". Likewise His saying: ﴿حتّى إِذَا أَثْخَنْتُموهمْ فَشُدُّوا﴾ is referred back [177/b] to an implied command that puts ضرب الرقاب in the accusative.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿كَرِهُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ﴾: they disliked the Qurʾān and were displeased with it.

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿دَمَّرَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلِلْكَافِرِينَ أَمْثَالُهَا﴾: he says: for the people of Mecca [there are] the likes of what struck the people of Lot, ʿĀd and Thamūd; a threat from Allah.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَوْلَى ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾: He means: the protector (walī) of those who believe; and so it is in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "ذلك بأن الله ولِىّ الذين آمنوا". It is like the one in al-Māʾida in our reading: ﴿إنما وَلِيّكم اللهُ ورسولُه﴾, and their meaning is one, and Allah knows best.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلنَّارُ مَثْوًى لَّهُمْ﴾.
You put النار in the nominative by المثوى; and had you put المثوى in the accusative and النار in the nominative by the lām in (لهم), it would have been a valid view.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿مِّن قَرْيَتِكَ ٱلَّتِيۤ أَخْرَجَتْكَ﴾.
He means: whose people drove you out to Medina; and had it been من قريتك التى أخرجوك, it would have been a valid view, as He said: ﴿فَجاءَها بَأْسُنَا بَيَاتاً أَوْ هُمْ قائلون﴾: He said (قائلون), while at the beginning of the phrase [He said] (فجاءها).
His saying: ﴿فَلاَ نَاصِرَ لَهُمْ﴾.
It came in the exegesis: they had no helper when We destroyed them; and this is one view. Implying كان is also allowed, even though you have put الناصر in the accusative by the [lā of] absolute negation (tabriya). And it may be: We destroyed them, so they have no helper now from the punishment of Allah.

farraa:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿أَفَمَن كَانَ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ كَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوۤءُ عَمَلِهِ وَٱتَّبَعُوۤاْ أَهْوَاءَهُمْ﴾, and He did not say واتبع هواه. That is because مَن may be in the meaning of one and of many, so أهواؤهم was referred back to the meaning. Like it: ﴿وَمِنَ الشياطِينِ مَنْ يَغُوصُون له﴾; and in another place: ﴿ومِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمعُ إِلَيكَ﴾; and in another place: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ﴾.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿مَّثَلُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِي وُعِدَ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī informed me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "the likeness of Paradise" means the likenesses of Paradise, the descriptions of Paradise. Ibn ʿAbbās said: and so ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib read it: أمثال.
His saying: ﴿مِّن مَّآءٍ غَيْرِ آسِنٍ﴾.
Unchanging, not stale.
His saying: ﴿وَأَنْهَارٌ مِّن لَّبَنٍ لَّمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ طَعْمُهُ﴾: it did not come out of the udders of camels or sheep with its froth.
His saying: ﴿وَأَنْهَارٌ مِّنْ خَمْرٍ لَّذَّةٍ لِّلشَّارِبِينَ﴾.
لذة is in the genitive, and it is the wine itself; and if you wish, you make it follow الأنهار: "and rivers, delightful (لذةٌ)"; and if you wish, you put it in the accusative on [the sense]: "it is delighted in as a delight (لذةً)", as you say: "This is yours as a gift (هبةً)" and the like. Then He said: ﴿كَمَنْ هُوَ خَالِدٌ﴾: He did not say: "Is the one who is in this like one who abides in the Fire?", but that meaning is in it, so it was built upon it.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ﴾.
He means your sermon on Friday [178/a]: they do not listen and do not take it in, [until], when they leave and the people go out, they say to the Muslims: "What did he say just now?", meaning the Prophet, Allah bless him and grant him peace, mocking.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿أُولئك الَّذِينَ طَبعَ اللهُ على قُلوبهم﴾.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱهْتَدَوْاْ زَادَهُمْ هُدًى﴾.
Their mocking increased them in guidance, and Allah gave them their piety. It is said: He rewarded them with the reward of their piety; it is said: He inspired them with their piety; and it is said: He gave them their piety [in avoiding] the abrogated when the abrogating was revealed.
«[Translator's note: "their mocking increased them in guidance" is what the source says; the sense is presumably that the hypocrites' mocking increased the guided ones in guidance.]»

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿فَهَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ بَغْتَةً فَقَدْ جَآءَ أَشْرَاطُهَا﴾.
(أنْ) has fatḥa in all the readings. Al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Abū Jaʿfar al-Ruʾāsī narrated to me, saying: I said to Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ: "What is this fāʾ in His saying: ﴿فَقَدْ جَآءَ أَشْرَاطُهَا﴾?" He said: "A response to the requital (jazāʾ)." He said: I said: "But it is ﴿أَنْ تأتيهم﴾ with fatḥa?" He said: he said: "Allah forbid! It is only (إِنْ تَأْتِهِمْ)." Al-Farrāʾ said: I thought he took it from the people of Mecca, because he read with them. It is also in some codices of the Kufans: تأتهم, with a single tooth [i.e. without the yāʾ], but none of them read it so. It is of repetition (mukarrar): "Do they await anything but the Hour; do they await anything but that it come to them suddenly?" The proof of that is that the one in al-Zukhruf in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh is: ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرونَ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَأْتيهم الساعةُ﴾. Like it: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ رِجالٌ مُؤْمِنُونَ وَنِساءٌ مؤمِناتٌ﴾ ... "لولا أن تطئوهم", where أن with fatḥa is in the position of the nominative; and أن in al-Zukhruf and here is accusative, referred back to الساعة. The jussive is allowed: you make "Do they await anything but the Hour" self-sufficient, then begin: إن تأتهم, and bring it with the fāʾ as the requital; and the jussive is allowed.
His saying: ﴿فَأَنَّىٰ لَهُمْ إِذَا جَآءَتْهُمْ ذِكْرَاهُمْ﴾.
"ذكراهم" is in the position of the nominative by لهم, and the meaning is: how will their remembrance avail them when the Hour comes to them? Like it: ﴿يَوْمَئذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ الإِنْسانُ وأنّى لَهُ الذِّكْرَى﴾, i.e. his remembering and his regret will not benefit him.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإِذَآ أُنزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ مُّحْكَمَةٌ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: سُورةٌ مُحْدَثةٌ. When a verse was revealed with fighting and the mention of it in it, it was hard on the Muslims, and they longed for it to be abrogated. That is His saying: "لولا نزلت سورة", i.e. why has a [sūra] other than this not been sent down? And when it was revealed and they were commanded to fight in it, they disliked it. Allah said: ﴿فَأَوْلَىٰ لَهُمْ﴾, for whoever disliked it. Then He described their saying before it was sent down: "Hearing and obedience"; they would say: "Hearing and obedience", and when the command came down they disliked it; had they been true to Allah, it would have been better for them. Al-ṭāʿa (obedience) is nominative in the speech of the Arabs: when they are told: "Do such-and-such", whether it weighs on them or not, they say: "Hearing and obedience (سمع وطاعة)". [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān informed me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَأَوْلَىٰ﴾, then said: "for those of them who believed: obedience and a fitting word". So فأولى became a threat for whoever disliked it, and He began anew with obedience for them. The first is, in our view, the speech of the Arabs, and this saying of al-Kalbī is not to be rejected.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: [178/b] ﴿فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ﴾.
The generality read it with fatḥa on the sīn, and Nāfiʿ of Medina read it: فهل عَسِيْتُم, with kasra on the sīn; and had it been so, he would have said عَسِىَ [in place of عسى]. Perhaps it is a rare dialect. The Arabs sometimes venture to alter some of the language when the verb is one that قد does not reach: they have said لُسْتُم, meaning لستُم, then they say ليس and ليسوا all the same, because it is a verb that does not inflect, having no imperfect (yafʿal); and likewise عسى has no imperfect, so perhaps he ventured on it as one ventured on لستم.
His saying: "هَلْ عَسَيْتُم" ...: if you take charge of the affairs of the people, that you will cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship. And it is said: perhaps, if you turn away from Muḥammad, Allah bless him and grant him peace, and turn your backs on him, you will revert to your former state of severing kinship, unbelief and corruption.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلشَّيْطَانُ سَوَّلَ لَهُمْ﴾.
He made it seem fair to them, and Allah gave them respite (أملى لهم); and so al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read it, and it is reported of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ibn Masʿūd and Zayd ibn Thābit (may Allah have mercy on them) that they read it so, with fatḥa on the alif.
And it is reported of Mujāhid that he read it: (وأُمْلىِ لهم), with the yāʾ unvowelled, Allah, Majestic and Mighty, informing about Himself ("and I give them respite"); and some of the people of Medina read: وأُمْلِىَ لهم, with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the alif, making it a passive verb whose agent is not named; and the meaning is close.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿إِسْرَارَهُمْ﴾.
The people read it: أسرارهم, the plural of sirr (secret); and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb alone read it: إسرارهم, with kasra on the alif, and al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī followed him; and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Like it: ﴿وإِدْبَارَ السجود﴾.

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿أَن لَّن يُخْرِجَ ٱللَّهُ أَضْغَانَهُمْ﴾: he says: that Allah will not reveal their enmity and their hatred for Muḥammad, Allah bless him.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لأَرَيْنَاكَهُمْ﴾.
He means: We would have made them known to you. You say to a man: "I have shown you such-and-such", and its meaning is: I have made it known to you and taught it to you. Like it: ﴿وَلَتَعْرِفَنَّهُمْ فِى لَحْنِ الْقَوْلِ﴾: in the manner (naḥw) of speech and in the meaning of speech.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلاَ تَهِنُواْ وَتَدْعُوۤاْ إِلَى ٱلسَّلْمِ﴾.
Both are jussive by the prohibition: "do not weaken and do not call". It may also be accusative by diversion (ṣarf). He says: do not call to al-salm, which is peace-making, while you are the uppermost: you are the victors; the outcome is yours.
His saying: ﴿وَلَن يَتِرَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ﴾.
From "I wronged (watartu) the man": when you killed one of his people or took property from him, you have watartahu. It came in the ḥadīth: "Whoever misses the ʿaṣr prayer, it is as though he were deprived (wutira) of his family and his property." Al-Farrāʾ said: and some of the jurists say أوتر, but the correct form is وتر.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿إِن يَسْأَلْكُمُوهَا فَيُحْفِكُمْ﴾.
I.e. He presses you hard, you become stingy, and He brings out your rancour; and that stinginess brings out your enmity. And it may be: Allah brings out your rancour. "I pressed (aḥfaytu) the man": I strained him.

zajjaj:34-34.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ ماتُوا وهم كُفّارٌ فَلَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ﴾: He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He does not forgive whoever dies in disbelief.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلا تَهِنُوا وتَدْعُوا إلى السَّلْمِ﴾ — and "اَلسَّلَمِ" — its meaning is peace (reconciliation). Peace is called "السِّلْمُ", "السَّلْمُ" and "السَّلَمُ". The meaning of "لا تَهِنُوا" is: do not weaken; one says "وَهَنَ، يَهِنُ" when someone becomes weak. So Allah forbade the Muslims to invite the disbelievers to peace, and commanded them to fight them until they submit to Islam.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأنْتُمُ الأعْلَوْنَ واللَّهُ مَعَكُمْ﴾: its interpretation is: you are the uppermost in the argument, and with you is the Prophet ﷺ and the signs he brought which prove his prophethood; ﴿واللَّهُ مَعَكُمْ﴾, that is: your Helper.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَنْ يَتِرَكم أعْمالَكُمْ﴾, that is: He will not diminish for you anything of your reward.

zajjaj:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنْ تُؤْمِنُوا وتَتَّقُوا يُؤْتِكم أُجُورَكُمْ﴾ — and He had made known to them that their reward is the Garden — ﴿وَلا يَسْألْكم أمْوالَكُمْ﴾ ﴿إنْ يَسْألْكُمُوها فَيُحْفِكم تَبْخَلُوا﴾ [Muḥammad: 37], that is: if He were to exhaust you by asking, you would be miserly, "ويُخْرِجْ أضْغانَكُمْ" (and He would bring out your rancour) — and "نُخْرِجْ أضْغانَكُمْ" (and We would bring out your rancour); it has been read both ways.

zajjaj:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا يَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْمًا غَيْرَكم ثُمَّ لا يَكُونُوا أمْثالَكُمْ﴾: It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis): if the servants turn away, Allah will replace them with the angels. It has also come: if the people of Mecca turn away, Allah will replace them with the people of Medina. It has also come: He will replace you with a people other than you from the people of Persia. As for what has come, that He will replace them with the angels, in the language — as far as I suppose — it is far-fetched, because the angels are not called "قَوْمٌ" (a people); "قَوْمٌ" is said only of human beings. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: if you turn away, He will replace you with a people more obedient than you, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿عَسى رَبُّهُ إنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ أنْ يُبْدِلَهُ أزْواجًا خَيْرًا مِنكُنَّ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 5], to the end of the story; and not all the people turned away — and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat "Muḥammad" ﷺ
Meccan
«[Translator's note: the source labels the sura Meccan; it is generally counted as Medinan.]»
﷽
﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أضَلَّ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أضَلَّ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾: He rendered them void, so they see no reward for them in the Hereafter. The meaning is that whatever charity, upholding of kinship ties and kinds of good deeds they had done was rendered void by their disbelief, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُرِيهِمُ اللَّهُ أعْمالَهم حَسَراتٍ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 167], and His saying: ﴿كَسَرابٍ بِقِيعَةٍ﴾ [al-Nūr: 39]. These are the ones who turned [people] away from the Prophet ﷺ. The proof of that is His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ وآمَنُوا بِما نُـزِّلَ عَلى مُحَمَّدٍ وهو الحَقُّ مِن رَبِّهِمْ كَفَّرَ عَنْهم سَيِّئاتِهِمْ وأصْلَحَ بالَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 2], that is, He expiated for them what they had committed while they were disbelievers, when they believed in Allah, in the Prophet, peace be upon him, and in all the other prophets.

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأصْلَحَ بالَهُمْ﴾: that is, He set right their affairs and their condition.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا اتَّبَعُوا الباطِلَ﴾: that is, "the matter is that, because those who disbelieved followed falsehood." It is also possible that [the meaning is]: that leading astray is because of their following falsehood, and that guidance and those expiations are because of the believers' following the truth. Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ لِلنّاسِ أمْثالَهُمْ﴾, that is, thus Allah makes clear to people the likenesses of the good deeds of the believers and the evil deeds of the disbelievers, that is, like the clarification that has been mentioned. The meaning of someone's saying "ضَرَبْتُ لَكَ مَثَلًا" is: I have made clear to you a kind (ḍarb) of likeness, that is, a type of them.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإذا لَقِيتُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَضَرْبَ الرِّقابِ﴾: its meaning is: strike the necks with striking; it is accusative as a command. Its interpretation is: when you meet those who disbelieve, kill them; but most occurrences of killing are by striking the neck, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, taught them how to aim, and how He said: ﴿واضْرِبُوا مِنهم كُلَّ بَنانٍ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 12]; that is, it is not to be imagined from this that striking is forbidden except on the neck alone.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتّى إذا أثْخَنْتُمُوهم فَشُدُّوا الوَثاقَ﴾: "أثْخَنْتُمُوهُمْ" means: you have inflicted much slaughter among them, as He said: ﴿ما كانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ أسْرى حَتّى يُثْخِنَ في الأرْضِ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 67]. So taking captives comes after thoroughness in killing. Then He said: ﴿فَإمّا مَنًّا بَعْدُ وإمّا فِداءً﴾, that is, after you take them captive, either you grant them freedom as a favour, or you release them for ransom.
And His saying: ﴿حَتّى تَضَعَ الحَرْبُ أوْزارَها﴾: "حَتّى" is connected to the killing and the taking of captives; the meaning is: kill them and take them captive until the war lays down its burdens. The exegesis is: until they believe and submit, so that it is not obligatory for you to fight them; as long as disbelief remains, jihād and war remain standing for ever.
And His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ ولَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ لانْتَصَرَ مِنهُمْ﴾: "ذَلِكَ" is in the position of the nominative, the meaning being "the matter is that"; it may also be accusative with the meaning "do that." ﴿وَلَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ لانْتَصَرَ مِنهُمْ﴾: that is, if Allah willed He would punish them and destroy them, because He is able to do that. ﴿وَلَكِنْ لِيَبْلُوَ بَعْضَكم بِبَعْضٍ﴾: the meaning is: but He commanded you to fight in order to test some of you by means of others, that is, so that Allah may purify the believers and obliterate the disbelievers.
And His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَلَنْ يُضِلَّ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾: He mentioned at the beginning of the sura: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أضَلَّ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 1], and He made known that those who fight in the way of Allah, He will not let their deeds go astray. It is read in four ways: "قاتَلُوا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ" (they fought), and "قُتِلُوا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ" (they were killed), in the passive (mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu); it is read "قُتِّلُوا" with the tāʾ doubled; and it is read "قَتَلُوا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ" (they killed), with fatḥa on the qāf.

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying: ﴿سَيَهْدِيهِمْ ويُصْلِحُ بالَهُمْ﴾: He will set right for them the affairs of their livelihood in this world, along with what He will reward them with in the Hereafter, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّهم أقامُوا التَّوْراةَ والإنْجِيلَ وما أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْهِمْ مِن رَبِّهِمْ لأكَلُوا مِن فَوْقِهِمْ ومِن تَحْتِ أرْجُلِهِمْ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 66], that is, had they accepted what is in them and in the [other] books and acted upon it, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet; and as He said: ﴿اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكم إنَّهُ كانَ غَفّارًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 10] ﴿يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكم مِدْرارًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 11] ﴿وَيُمْدِدْكم بِأمْوالٍ وبَنِينَ ويَجْعَلْ لَكم جَنّاتٍ ويَجْعَلْ لَكم أنْهارًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 12]. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, promised the believers the setting right of their affairs and their condition in this world and the Hereafter.

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَتَعْسًا لَهم وأضَلَّ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾: "اَلَّذِينَ" is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and ﴿فَتَعْسًا لَهُمْ﴾ is the khabar (predicate). It may also be accusative with the meaning "Allah has made them wretched." "اَلتَّعْسُ" in the language means falling down and stumbling.

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهم كَرِهُوا ما أنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأحْبَطَ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾: they hated the Qur'an and the prophethood of the Prophet, peace be upon him, so Allah rendered their deeds void.

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا في الأرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾: the meaning is: so that they might see what the end was of the disbelievers who were before them. ﴿دَمَّرَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: that is, Allah destroyed them. ﴿وَلِلْكافِرِينَ أمْثالُها﴾: that is, the like of that end. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, destroyed by the sword those whom He destroyed of those who turned [people] away from the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: that is, because Allah is the protector (walī) of those who believe; He takes charge of them in all their affairs, in guiding them and in victory over their enemy. ﴿وَأنَّ الكافِرِينَ لا مَوْلى لَهُمْ﴾: that is, they have no protector to help them against Allah, neither in guidance nor in prevailing over the believers. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known what He has prepared for the believers, along with victory and establishment, and what He has prepared for the disbelievers, along with forsaking and leading astray, and said: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ﴾ [Muḥammad: 12].

zajjaj:12-12.t: Then He explained the attributes of those gardens, and said: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يَتَمَتَّعُونَ ويَأْكُلُونَ كَما تَأْكُلُ الأنْعامُ والنّارُ مَثْوًى لَهُمْ﴾. "اَلْمَثْوى" means the abode.

zajjaj:13-13.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَأيِّنْ مِن قَرْيَةٍ هي أشَدُّ قُوَّةً مِن قَرْيَتِكَ الَّتِي أخْرَجَتْكَ أهْلَكْناهُمْ﴾: the meaning is: "How many people of a town, stronger in power than the people of your town which drove you out" — that is, those who drove you out — "We destroyed for their denying the messengers," ﴿فَلا ناصِرَ لَهُمْ﴾.

zajjaj:14-14.t: Then He made known, and said: ﴿أفَمَن كانَ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِن رَبِّهِ كَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ واتَّبَعُوا أهْواءَهُمْ﴾: This is an alif of bringing [the listener] to a halt (tawqīf) and eliciting acknowledgement (taqrīr), because the answer is known; just as when you say: "Whoever does evil deeds will be wretched, and whoever does good deeds will be happy," and then say: "Is wretchedness dearer to you, or happiness?", it is known that the answer is "happiness." This is the way the alif of tawqīf and taqrīr works.

zajjaj:15-15.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَثَلُ الجَنَّةِ﴾ is an explanation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ﴾ [Muḥammad: 12]. He explained those rivers, and said: ﴿مَثَلُ الجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ المُتَّقُونَ﴾, that is, [the likeness], from what you know of the gardens and rivers of this world, is a garden: ﴿فِيها أنْهارٌ مِن ماءٍ غَيْرِ آسِنٍ﴾. It is also read "مِن ماءٍ غَيْرِ أسِنٍ", and "أسْنٍ" is permissible in Arabic. One says "أسَنَ الماءُ، يَأْسِنُ، فَهو آسِنٌ", and one says "أسَنَ الماءُ، فَهو أسِنٌ", when its smell has changed. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the smell of the water of the rivers of Paradise does not change and it does not become stale. ﴿وَأنْهارٌ مِن لَبَنٍ لَمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ طَعْمُهُ﴾: that is, the change that affects the milk of this world does not enter it. ﴿وَأنْهارٌ مِن خَمْرٍ لَذَّةٍ لِلشّارِبِينَ﴾: there is no ghawl (harm) in it, that is, it does not intoxicate and does not run out. ﴿وَأنْهارٌ مِن عَسَلٍ مُصَفًّى﴾: its meaning is: purified; it has not come out of the bellies of bees so that wax mixes with it. ﴿وَلَهم فِيها مِن كُلِّ الثَّمَراتِ﴾: as He said: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ﴾ [Muḥammad: 12]; He described those gardens, saying: "مَثَلُ الجَنَّةِ جَنَّةٌ…" (the likeness of the Garden is a garden…), as He described. It has also been said that the meaning is: "the description (ṣifa) of the Garden," which is close to what we have explained. Then He said: ﴿وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِن رَبِّهِمْ﴾, that is, they have in it of all fruits, and they have forgiveness from their Lord: He forgives their sins, and they are not requited for evil deeds nor rebuked in Paradise, so that it is the great triumph and the abundant gift. Then He said: ﴿كَمَن هو خالِدٌ في النّارِ وسُقُوا ماءً حَمِيمًا فَقَطَّعَ أمْعاءَهُمْ﴾; the meaning is: Is the one who stands upon clear proof from his Lord, and is given these things, like the one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, and who abides eternally in the Fire?! ﴿وَسُقُوا ماءً حَمِيمًا فَقَطَّعَ أمْعاءَهُمْ﴾: the singular of "الأمْعاءِ" (intestines) is "مِعًى", like "ضِلَعٌ" and "أضْلاعٌ".

zajjaj:16-16.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنهم مَن يَسْتَمِعُ إلَيْكَ﴾: He means the hypocrites. ﴿حَتّى إذا خَرَجُوا مِن عِنْدِكَ قالُوا لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا العِلْمَ ماذا قالَ آنِفًا﴾: they used to listen to the sermon of the Prophet ﷺ, and when they went out they asked the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, in mockery and to make known that they had paid no attention to what he said: "What did he say just now?" — that is, what did he say a moment ago. The meaning of "آنِفًا" comes from your saying "اسْتَأْنَفْتُ الشَّيْءَ" (I began the thing anew) when you begin it, and "رَوْضَةٌ أُنُفٌ" (a fresh meadow) when it has not yet been grazed, that is, it has a first grazing still to come. So the meaning is: what did he say at the earliest time close to us?
And His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ واتَّبَعُوا أهْواءَهُمْ﴾ ﴿والَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا زادَهم هُدًى﴾ [Muḥammad: 17]: the pronoun in "زادَهم" may have one of three aspects. The best of them — and Allah knows best — is that it refers to Allah, so the meaning goes back to His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ واتَّبَعُوا أهْواءَهُمْ﴾ ﴿والَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا زادَهم هُدًى﴾ [Muḥammad: 17]. It is possible that the pronoun in "زادَهم" is the saying of the Messenger ﷺ, so the meaning would be: "And those who are guided, what the Messenger of Allah said increases them in guidance." And it is possible that the hypocrites' turning away and mockery increased them in guidance.
His saying: ﴿وَآتاهم تَقْواهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 17]: it may be "and He inspired them with their God-fearing," as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَألْزَمَهم كَلِمَةَ التَّقْوى وكانُوا أحَقَّ بِها وأهْلَها﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 26]; and it may be — and Allah knows best — "and He gave them the reward of their God-fearing."

zajjaj:18-18.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إلا السّاعَةَ أنْ تَأْتِيَهم بَغْتَةً﴾: It is also read "إلّا السّاعَةَ إنْ تَأْتِهِمْ", without the yāʾ; the first is better, because it agrees with the codex. The position of "أنْ" is accusative as a badal (substitute) for "السّاعَةَ"; the meaning is: "Are they waiting for anything but that the Hour should come upon them suddenly?" This is the badal that includes the first in meaning (badal al-ishtimāl), like His saying ﴿وَلَوْلا رِجالٌ مُؤْمِنُونَ ونِساءٌ مُؤْمِناتٌ لَمْ تَعْلَمُوهم أنْ تَطَئُوهُمْ﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 25], the meaning being: "Were it not that you would trample believing men and believing women." The meaning of "هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ" and "هَلْ يَنْتَظِرُونَ" is the same. Whoever reads "إنْ تَأْتِهِمْ بَغْتَةً فَقَدْ جاءَ أشْراطُها", it is on [the pattern of] condition and requital (sharṭ and jazāʾ). "أشْراطُها" means its signs. ﴿فَأنّى لَهم إذا جاءَتْهم ذِكْراهُمْ﴾: the meaning is: "Whence will they have their remembrance when the Hour comes to them?!" "ذِكْراهُمْ" is in the position of the nominative by His saying "فَأنّى".

zajjaj:19-19.t: And His saying: ﴿فاعْلَمْ أنَّهُ لا إلَهَ إلا اللَّهُ﴾: this fāʾ came for the requital (jazāʾ); the meaning is: "We have made clear what shows that Allah is One," so Allah made known that there is no god but Allah. The Prophet, peace be upon him, already knew that, but it is an address in which people are included together with the Prophet ﷺ, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ إذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 1]. The meaning is: "Whoever knows, let him remain steadfast upon that knowledge," as He said: ﴿اهْدِنا الصِّراطَ المُسْتَقِيمَ﴾ [al-Fātiḥa: 6], that is, keep us firm upon guidance. ﴿واللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مُتَقَلَّبَكم ومَثْواكُمْ﴾: that is, He knows your movements and He knows your abode, that is, He knows where your place of residence is in this world and the Hereafter.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَوْلا نُـزِّلَتْ سُورَةٌ﴾: The believers, may Allah have mercy on them, used to find comfort in revelation and to feel desolate when it was slow in coming; that is why they said: ﴿لَوْلا نُـزِّلَتْ سُورَةٌ﴾.
﴿فَإذا أُنْـزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ مُحْكَمَةٌ وذُكِرَ فِيها القِتالُ﴾: the meaning of "مُحْكَمَةٌ" is: not abrogated. So when the obligation of fighting is mentioned in it, ﴿رَأيْتَ الَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾ — meaning the hypocrites — ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ إلَيْكَ نَظَرَ المَغْشِيِّ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ المَوْتِ﴾, because they are hypocrites who hate fighting, since if they stayed back from it their hypocrisy would become manifest, and so they feared being killed. ﴿فَأوْلى لَهُمْ﴾: "أوْلى لَهُمْ" is a threat and a menace; the meaning is: what is hateful is close upon them (waliyahum).

zajjaj:21-21.t:
And His saying: ﴿طاعَةٌ وقَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ﴾: Sībawayh and al-Khalīl said: the meaning is "obedience and a fitting word would be better (amthal)." It has been said that their saying at first was: "Obedience and a fitting word." And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that the meaning is: "So when a sura is sent down possessing obedience — that is, in which obedience is commanded — and a fitting word," so the meaning would be: "So when a sura is sent down possessing obedience and a fitting word."
﴿فَإذا عَزَمَ الأمْرُ فَلَوْ صَدَقُوا اللَّهَ لَكانَ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ﴾: the meaning is: when the matter became serious and the obligation of fighting became binding, had they been true to Allah — believing in the Prophet ﷺ and acting on what was revealed to him and what they were commanded of the obligation of fighting — it would have been better for them; the meaning is: their being true to Allah through their faith would have been better for them.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ﴾: Nāfiʿ read "فَهَلْ عَسِيتُمْ", but the good, eloquent usage is "عَسَيْتُمْ", with fatḥa on the sīn; were "عَسِيتُمْ" permissible, it would be permissible to say "عَسِيَ رَبُّكم أنْ يَرْحَمَكُمْ". It is also read "أنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ", and "إنْ تُوُلِّيتُمْ", with ḍamma on the tāʾ, and with fatḥa. ﴿أنْ تُفْسِدُوا في الأرْضِ وتُقَطِّعُوا أرْحامَكُمْ﴾: whoever reads "تَوَلَّيْتُمْ" with fatḥa, there are two aspects in it. One of them is that the meaning is: "Perhaps, if you turn away from what the Prophet brought you, you would return to the affairs of the Jāhiliyya, and cause corruption, and kill one another," ﴿وَتُقَطِّعُوا أرْحامَكُمْ﴾, that is, bury daughters alive. And it may be: "Perhaps, if you take charge of the affair (tawallaytum al-amr), you would cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship, and Quraysh would kill Banū Hāshim and Banū Hāshim Quraysh; and likewise if you are put in charge (tuwullītum)."
«[Translator's note: the final clause "وكَذَلِكَ إنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ" is printed with the same form "تَوَلَّيْتُمْ"; the reference to the passive reading is the translator's inference.]»

zajjaj:25-25.t:
And His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ ارْتَدُّوا عَلى أدْبارِهِمْ مِن بَعْدِ ما تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الهُدى﴾: the meaning is: they returned to disbelief after hearing the guidance and its becoming clear.
And His saying: ﴿الشَّيْطانُ سَوَّلَ لَهم وأمْلى لَهُمْ﴾: the meaning of ﴿سَوَّلَ لَهُمْ﴾ is: made attractive to them. ﴿وَأمْلى لَهُمْ﴾: Allah granted them respite, as He said: ﴿إنَّما نُمْلِي لَهم لِيَزْدادُوا إثْمًا﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 178], meaning: We only defer them. It has been read "اَلشَّيْطانُ سَوَّلَ لَهم وأُمْلِي لَهُمْ", as a statement from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, the meaning being "and I grant respite"; and it has been read "وَأُمْلِيَ لَهُمْ", with fatḥa on the yāʾ, in the passive (mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu).

zajjaj:26-26.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهم قالُوا لِلَّذِينَ كَرِهُوا ما نَـزَّلَ اللَّهُ سَنُطِيعُكم في بَعْضِ الأمْرِ﴾: the meaning — and Allah knows best — is "the matter is that," that is, "that leading astray is because of their saying to those who hated what Allah sent down." It has come in the exegesis that they are the Jews, who said: "We will obey you in part of the matter," that is, we will obey you in backing one another in enmity towards the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿واللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إسْرارَهُمْ﴾, and "أسْرارَهُمْ" — both have been read. Whoever reads "أسْرارَهُمْ" with fatḥa, it is the plural of "سِرٌّ" (secret), "أسْرارٌ", like "حِمْلٌ" and "أحْمالٌ"; and whoever reads ﴿إسْرارَهُمْ﴾, it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "أسْرَرْتُ، إسْرارًا" (I kept secret).

zajjaj:27-27.t: And His saying: ﴿فَكَيْفَ إذا تَوَفَّتْهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهم وأدْبارَهُمْ﴾: they do that to them in the fire of Hell — and Allah knows best. And the meaning may be: how will their state be when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs?

zajjaj:28-28.t: His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهُمُ اتَّبَعُوا ما أسْخَطَ اللَّهَ وكَرِهُوا رِضْوانَهُ﴾: the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "That is their requital, because they followed the thing that angered Allah and hated His good pleasure," that is, they followed those who opposed the Prophet ﷺ and those who opposed the Sharīʿa, and hated faith in the Prophet ﷺ and following his Sharīʿa. ﴿فَأحْبَطَ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾: that is, whatever good deeds there were, such as upholding kinship, kindness or charity, Allah rendered that void by their disbelief in what the Prophet ﷺ brought.

zajjaj:29-29.t: And His saying: ﴿أمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ أنْ لَنْ يُخْرِجَ اللَّهُ أضْغانَهُمْ﴾: "اَلَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ" are the hypocrites; that is, "that Allah would not reveal their enmity towards His Messenger, peace be upon him, and make him aware of their hypocrisy."

zajjaj:30-30.t:
﴿وَلَوْ نَشاءُ لأرَيْناكَهُمْ﴾: the meaning of ﴿لأرَيْناكَهُمْ﴾ is: We would have made them known to you. You say "قَدْ أرَيْتُكَ هَذا الأمْرَ", that is, I have made you acquainted with it. The meaning is: "If We willed, We would put a mark on the hypocrites," and that is "al-sīmiyāʾ" (the distinguishing mark). ﴿فَلَعَرَفْتَهم بِسِيماهُمْ﴾: that is, by that mark. ﴿وَلَتَعْرِفَنَّهم في لَحْنِ القَوْلِ﴾: that is, in the drift of speech. By this He indicated — and Allah knows best — that a speaker's words and deeds indicate his intention. People's saying "قَدْ لَحَنَ فُلانٌ" is interpreted as: he has taken a direction away from what is correct and turned aside from the correct to it. And the poet's saying:
مَنطِقٌ صائِبٌ وتَلْحَنُ أحْيا ∗∗∗ نًا وخَيْرُ الحَدِيثِ ما كانَ لَحْنا
(Speech that hits the mark, and at times she speaks by allusion; and the best talk is that which is allusive.)
Its interpretation is: "The best talk from one such as her is that which not everyone understands; her words are understood only through the turns of her speech."

zajjaj:31-31.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكم حَتّى نَعْلَمَ المُجاهِدِينَ مِنكُمْ﴾: the meaning of "لَنَبْلُوَنَّكم" is: We will surely test you with war, ﴿حَتّى نَعْلَمَ المُجاهِدِينَ مِنكم والصّابِرِينَ﴾. He, Mighty and Majestic is He, knew before creating them those of them who would strive and those who would be patient; but He meant the knowledge upon which requital is based, because He requites them only for their deeds. So its interpretation is: "until He knows those who strive with a knowledge of witnessing (ʿilm shahāda)." He, Mighty and Majestic is He, knew the unseen, but requital with reward and punishment falls upon the knowledge of witnessing.
